 JUDGMENT

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petitions filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V.
Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- each due 3 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 to the injuries sustained by them, in a road traffic accident.
2. These two petitions are arising out of the same accident.
Hence, these petitions are clubbed and taken together for common discussion, for the sake of convenience and to avoid the repetition.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL *
3. Facts leading to the case of the petitioners forthcoming in the petition averments that, on the fateful date of the alleged accident, on 31.10.2022 at about 9.45 a.m., the petitioners were proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-52-R-2979, slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules and regulations, when they reached near Tumkur- Bengaluru NH-48 road,
near Budihal U turn, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala taluk, Bengaluru

, at that time, the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-GA- 9999, came from behind with high speed, in a rash 4 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 and negligent manner, and dashed against the motor cycle.
As a result, the petitioners were fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
4. It is stated in the petition that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner of MVC No.6313/2022, was shifted to Care Asia Hospital, wherein she took the treatment as an inpatient.
For her medical expenses and other incidental expenses, she had spent Rs.2,00,000/- and got permanent disability due to the injuries sustained by her.
5. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, petitioner of MVC 6312/2022, was shifted to Care Asia Hospital, wherein, the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient.
For her medical expenses and other incidental expenses, she had spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- and got permanent disability due to the injuries sustained by her.

student, studying at Shri Shivakumar Swamijji College of Engineering and also doing tailoring work and used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
And used to utilize the said amount, for the maintenance of her family.

Due to this, unfortunate accident, the petitioner has suffered mentally and physically,

7. It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner of MVC 6312/2022, was hale and healthy,
student, studying at Shri Shivakumar Swamijji College of Engineering and also doing tailoring work and used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month, and used to utilize the said amount, for the maintenance of her family.
Due to this, unfortunate accident, the petitioner had suffered both mentally and physically, as well as financially.
It is alleged in the petitions that, the alleged accident had taken place, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-GA-9999.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have filed both petitions claiming compensation in the case on hand.
9. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, respondent No.1 has not appeared through his counsel, remained absent, placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and file in answer to the case of the petitioner.

10. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, has not seriously disputed the accident, and the injuries sustained by the petitioners in the said 7 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 accident in question.

It is the main contention of the respondent No.2 that, alleged accident was not due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, as the accident had occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-52-R-2979.
But, admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-41-GA-9999, and the same was valid from 24.9.2022 to 23.9.2023.

Further contended that,
neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) & Section 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.

Further contended that, driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle and the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these 8 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
11.

following issues were framed:

In continuation of the said discussion on perusal of the spot mahazar, along with spot sketch marked at Ex.P3 & Ex.P4, and the recitals of the said documents, executed by the investigation officer reflect about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, since the said documents were executed in presence of panch witnesses, there are no suspicious circumstances forthcoming to disbelieve the said documents, and also to police notice as well as reply to 15 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 the police notice.
Another material document IMV report marked at Ex.P7 reveals that, the alleged accident was not due to any mechanical defects involved in the accident.
Apart from this, Ex.P8 & Ex.P22 reveal that, both the petitioners had sustained grievous injuries on the history of RTA.

22. Ultimately, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Shankarappa Kunnal alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC, and the allegations made against the driver of the offending vehicle in column No.17 of the charge sheet, remained unshaken & uncontroverted by the other side.

Though the police papers are not substantive piece of evidence, in the absence of contra 16 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 materials, there is no hurdle to believe the said documents, as conclusive proof in connection with the above fact in issue.
23. Another point to be noted herein that, even at the time of cross-examination of PW1 & PW2,
though

several questions put to the witnesses by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, to the effect that, due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the defending vehicle, alleged accident and its consequences were taken place, in para No.2 and 3 of the cross-examination of PW1, and in para No.2 of the cross-examination of PW2, nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the allegations made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence, I am of the view that both the petitioners have placed cogent and convincing evidence in support of the above issue, and no rebuttal evidence to disbelieve and to suspect the case of the petitioners.

In the light of the evidence placed on record, by way of affidavit evidence and the documentary evidence, speak that, the petitioners have paced satisfactory evidence to prove the above issues, to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41-GA-9999.

Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1,
in both the cases are in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 IN BOTH THE CASES :

Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioners about the injuries sustained by them, in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavour to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

Firstly, in connection with the MVC No.6313/2022 is concerned, the petitioner by name Meghana R., to substantiate her contention that, she 19 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 had sustained injuries in the accident, has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P8.

The said document discloses that, he sustained the following injuries:-
1) Fracture Navicular bone (right) foot 2) CLW over face & foot 28.
According to the doctor, the aforesaid injury No.1 is grievous in nature and the injury No.2 is simple in nature.
Apart from this, the petitioner had produced discharge summary, prescriptions, medical bills, lab report, x-ray as per Ex.P16 to Ex.P20.

On going through the discharge summary of Care Asia Hospital,
Nelamangala as per Ex.P16 reveals that the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient from 30.10.2022 to 1.11.2022.

For having taken note of the injury and the treatment taken by the petitioner, it is apt to consider the compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.

In the petition, she had stated that, prior to the accident, she was studying at Shri Shivakumar Swamiji College of Engineering and also doing tailoring and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, to substantiate the same, there is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner as Rs.20,000/- per month, as on the date of the accident.
On going through the discharge summary of Care Asia Hospital, Nelamangala as per Ex.P16 reveals that the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient from 30.10.2022 to 1.11.2022.

As such, during period of Kumari Neha Kouser.A vs Adgp State Intelligence on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179631822/
7 treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to her, to do daily routine work and to do her work for livelihood at least for one month.

30. The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence,
placed 16 medical bill as per Ex.P18 of Rs.42,065/- along with prescriptions as per Ex.P17.

In connection with the medical bills, the learned counsel for the respondent company had put some questions in the cross examination of the PW1, but no contra materials placed to disbelieve the bills furnished by the petitioner.
By looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.42,065/- towards medical expenses.

31. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, especially, the wound certificate and other medical documents and also on going through the evidence of PW1 and documents placed by her,
reflects 22 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 that, the petitioner had sustained grievous injury.

On going through medical documents placed on record, as discussed above, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.
32. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Except the production of medical documents, and averments made in the main petition, as well as in the chief affidavit, has not made an effort to examine the treated doctor, in order to prove the disability sustained by her, due to the accidental injuries in order to know, whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner, will affect to her future, and whether the said injuries will make any discomfort, to the petitioner to do her routine work as well as her work 23 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 for her avocation.
In such a situation, court cannot consider the loss of future income, in the absence of convincing evidence from the side of the petitioner, on the basis of surmises and conjunctures.
Hence, the petitioner has not made out acceptable grounds, to get the compensation under the head of loss of future income due to want of evidence on record.

33. Next factual aspect of loss of amenities is concerned, in the light of the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, definitely the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do her day to day work and for her work for avocation.
By taking into consideration of all these aspects, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities.
34. In connection with the future medication expenses is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any documents for consideration.
Hence, I am of the 24 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 view that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

44. Over all appreciation of entire medical documents, along with the evidence of PW1 in toto, I am of the view that, the percentage of disability in connection with whole body expressed by PW2,

45. In connection with the age of the petitioner by name Neha Kouser A. is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition, reveals that, as on the date of the petition, her age was 21 years.
In connection with the proof of age, she has placed Aadhar card as per Ex.P15, for consideration.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of 32 SCCH-18 MVC 6313/2022 & 6312/2022 the petitioner was mentioned as 9.6.2001.
The accident was occurred on 31.10.2022.
The said document remained unquestioned.
Hence, as on the date of accident, age of the petitioner was 21 years.
To the said age, as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.

46. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examination-in-chief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, she was studying in Shri Shivakumar Swamiji College of Engineering and also doing tailoring and was getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
